payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING auth-core-1 (high/security, confidence=high, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/server/src/auth/identity-routes.ts
LINES: 1305-1501

WHAT: Every other auth-surface handler in this router calls throttled(...) (apple-verify L602, google-verify L752, oidc L904, saml L1096, forgot-password L1671, reset-password L1781, refresh L1836), and the built-in /auth/login route in server.ts is throttled via authAttemptLimiter (server.ts L1485). But handleEmailLogin (L1433) and handleEmailSignup (L1305) contain NO throttled() call. The identity router is dispatched before the built-in routes (server.ts L1177), and /auth/email/login performs the same password verification (verifyAccountPassword, L1478) as the throttled /auth/login. An attacker can therefore brute-force passwords against /auth/email/login with no per-identifier/IP ceiling, sidestepping the exact FR-29 protection the codebase added for the other route. Signup is similarly unthrottled, enabling cheap account-spam / enumeration probing.

IMPACT: Unlimited online password-guessing against any email account, completely bypassing the FR-29 auth-attempt throttle that protects /auth/login. Argon2id cost slows each guess but does not bound attempt volume.

SUGGESTED FIX: Add throttled({ req, res, route: "email-login", identifier: email }) at the top of handleEmailLogin (after email is parsed) and throttled({ req, res, route: "email-signup", identifier: email }) in handleEmailSignup, mirroring the forgot-password/reset-password handlers.
